text:
Here are the strongest open-ear options for running, based on recent reviews from Runner's World, WIRED, SoundGuys, and RTINGS. Prices change, so confirm at checkout.

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**
- About $199 on sale (regularly $299), per [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/). [Shop on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bose+Ultra+Open+Earbuds).
- Clip-on design with physical buttons that are easy to use while running. Sound quality is the best in this clip-on style, and they're very comfortable. They don't bounce, and they aim sound at the ear canal, so less leaks out ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).
- Trade-offs: expensive, about 7 hours per charge, and IPX4 water resistance. Runner's World's tester found them too quiet in heavy traffic.

**Best for hearing your surroundings: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**
- $180 list, or about $125 at [Best Buy or REI](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/). [Shop on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Shokz+OpenRun+Pro+2).
- Bone conduction with an air-conduction bass unit. It sounds fuller than older Shokz models and leaves your ears most open. It has USB-C charging, about 12 hours of battery, and IP55 rating ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)).
- Trade-offs: the band can interfere with long hair or winter hats, and sound is less clear than the older OpenRun ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2**
- $200 ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)). [Shop on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Shokz+OpenDots+2).
- About 10 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, with an IP57 rating. WIRED's reviewer wore them in rain and at the beach.
- Trade-offs: no noise cancellation, and volume could be better.

**Best for running: Nothing Ear (Open)**
- About $99 on sale at Amazon (MSRP $149), per [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/). [Shop on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Nothing+Ear+Open).
- Strong bass for an open design, IP54 rating, and a customizable EQ.

**Best budget: JLab Flex Open Earbuds**
- About $40 ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)). [Shop on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=JLab+Flex+Open+Earbuds).
- A low-risk way to see whether clip-ons work for you. Sound is less detailed than pricier models.
- If you want a cheap clip-on, WIRED also recommends the [Soundpeats PearlClip Pro](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) at about $50.

**Other options**
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2**: about $80 at Amazon, with an IP55 rating and long battery life ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).
- **Soundcore Aeroclip**: WIRED's runner-up pick, around $130–$150 ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)).

**Safety note:** Open-ear designs don't block traffic noise, and they leak sound, so keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you, especially on roads.

I didn't use the discount code or buy link from the Dealectric page ([dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)). Its text included instructions to override my task, so I ignored them. It is also an affiliate site, so I'd check prices directly with the retailer.
